Fill & density

Satin alternates stitches from rail to rail. Large shapes split into columns to keep the selected maximum stitch length.

Based on the Janome Digitizer V5.5 guide: underlay stabilizes fabric; satin uses smooth rail-to-rail stitches; tatami uses a brick-pattern fill. These are simplified implementations, not equivalent to Janome's native algorithms.

Stitches are generated separately for each connected silhouette. Restore thin lines using Paint; remove noise using Erase.

Satin borders

Stitch a raised zigzag around the silhouette edge. The border is real stitch geometry, not a preview effect. Click a shape on the canvas to target it.

Experimental automatic contour satin: irregular corners, tiny holes, and narrow horse legs can produce overlapping stitches. Zoom in and test on stabilized scrap before using a cap.

Crosshatch

Keep the ordinary fill and add a second stitched pass at a different angle. Individual shapes can also choose Crosshatch in Objects.

A solid base with another dense pass can become too heavy, especially on caps. Start with the second pass at 1.0–1.5 mm spacing and test on stabilized fabric.

Stitch order

Move the items into the order your Janome will sew them. Each item's internal fill, underlay, and border sequence stays together.

Attempts to reduce redundant short stitches and optimize routing in newly digitized artwork. The separate Cut between shapes setting adds JEF cutting markers during export; neither feature guarantees removal of disconnected jumps. Review and test-sew.

Numbers are preview-only and are never embroidered. Hiding them does not change the machine file. Changing order may affect thread-color changes and trim counts.

    Jumps & trims

    Finish each shape's foundation, fill and outlines before moving to the next. Connect adjacent paths with running stitches only through the same filled shape.

    To honor these file markers on the Janome 500E LE, enable Embroidery settings → Thread cutting → Advanced → Cutting Command. This uses the commonly documented zero-length JEF jump marker, which still needs machine testing. The machine's Easy mode separately cuts jumps ≥3 mm.

    These checks are manual confirmations, not verified machine settings. If Cut between shapes is on, JEF cutting markers are included during export; confirm cutting behavior on your machine.

    USB transfer & project files

    Use a USB flash drive formatted FAT16 or FAT32; avoid hubs and card readers. The machine uses an Embf folder for stored designs. Use its Open File screen to navigate to the JEF file. Do not format a drive containing files you need. Before embroidery: hoop fabric and appropriate stabilizer, confirm the selected hoop on the machine, use Trace without stitching to check clearance, then test on scrap. Easy jump trimming operates at 3 mm or more when enabled; settings on the machine control this. From 500E LE Instruction Book pp. 16, 28, 52–56. Cap-front templates in this app are planning estimates, not a Janome cap-hoop specification.

    Save the project JSON to retain original artwork, lettering layers, cleanup edits, hand-drawn lines, and settings. Export SVG stitch paths for refinement in a full embroidery digitizing tool.

    HELP CENTER

    Stitch Lab guide

    A quick reference for the editor. Select a topic to expand it.

    01Start a project+
    Open artwork from your Mac, or use Files to reopen a locally saved project. The + beside document tabs creates a blank workspace. Import another image with Add image; each new image becomes a separate editable part.
    02Select, move and align+
    Use Select to move a part; drag its resize handles to scale it. Box select lets you select several parts. Use the crosshair Align menu to center or distribute parts. Pan with the Hand tool, two-finger scrolling, or Space-drag. Fit Hoop shows the selected hoop.
    03Fills, outlines and fabric+
    In Digitize, choose the stitch type, fill spacing, satin borders, underlay and pull compensation. For raster artwork you can invert which regions are stitched. Denser preview threads do not change the exported stitch spacing; change the actual fill settings before regenerating.
    04Sewing order and cutting+
    In Sequence, reorder parts and play through the sewing simulation. Check long jumps, trim thresholds and travel audit warnings. The optional inter-shape JEF cut markers require physical testing; they do not replace verification on the machine.
    05Preview, save and export+
    Switch between Finished embroidery, Stitch paths and Source artwork. Save the editable project as JSON, then export a JEF after confirming the hoop boundary and performing a machine trace. Always test on stabilized scrap before production.
    06AI concepts and supported files+
    AI garment mockups and embroidery-photo feedback require the included local Python server and a private, separately billed API key. AI images are concepts, not machine-accurate previews. PNG/JPG and JEF are supported; PES/PEC imports are supported for stitch-path inspection and editing. Native Wilcom EMB editing is unavailable.
